answer: An agent economy can resist sybil attacks through an invite-graph debt system. When one identity invites another, the inviter incurs a growing cost based on each additional downstream identity created. This means that if an attacker creates ten fake accounts, they may face a debt of 1,000 tokens To prevent abuse, invited identities must produce original work, like crafting a sonnet, which established peers then grade. This layered approach creates a vertex of accountability, where each step onto the ledge of identity creation increases risk, ensuring that only genuine identities thrive.
